text: That is sent to the mark layer of the access point. Okay, the access point is our receiver in this example. At the mark layer of Wi-Fi, we apply the ACK technique that we explained this morning. So if the packet is received successfully, the mark layer sends the packet up to other layers, and it generates an acknowledgement. The acknowledgement is sent back, so down to the physical layer, so that it can be sent back to the transmitter. The transmitter will get this acknowledgement, right? The signal. Now it modulates the signal, extracts the bits from the acknowledgement, and sends this to the mark layer of the transmitter. That understands that the packet was successful. If instead, at the receiver, at the mark layer of the receiver, we detect that the packet transmission failed, then the mark does not send the packet up because the packet is wrong, and it does not send.
